title: Hot Turkey Sandwich
subtitle: Open-faced roast turkey on toast with brown gravy
excerpt: Sliced roast turkey laid over white toast and smothered with a rich brown gravy. A diner classic that turns leftover turkey into a proper plate meal.
sourceNotes: American diner staple, popular across the Midwest and New England. Traditionally served open-faced with gravy ladled over the top.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: The gravy can be made 2 days ahead and refrigerated. Reheat gently and thin with a little stock if needed.

content.text: A hot turkey sandwich is an open-faced plate: toast, turkey, and gravy poured over the lot. The gravy carries the dish, so make it properly. Thin, pale gravy turns this into a sad meal.
Melt the butter in a medium saucepan over medium heat. Add the flour and stir constantly for 2 minutes until it smells nutty and turns a light golden colour.
Add the hot stock a splash at a time, whisking hard after each addition to keep the gravy smooth.
Once all the stock is in, bring to a gentle simmer. Cook for 8 minutes, stirring often, until the gravy coats the back of a spoon.
Add the Worcestershire sauce. Season with salt and black pepper. Keep warm over very low heat.
Lay 2 slices of toast on each plate. Arrange the turkey slices over the toast, overlapping slightly.
Ladle hot gravy generously over the turkey and toast. Serve at once with peas alongside.

items.cause: The stock was added too fast without whisking.
items.fix: Pass the gravy through a fine sieve and return it to the pan. Whisk over medium heat until smooth.

items.cause: Not enough simmering time, or the ratio of flour to stock was off.
items.fix: Simmer uncovered for 5 more minutes, stirring often. It will thicken as liquid evaporates.

items.symptom: The turkey is dry under the gravy.
items.cause: It was reheated separately and dried out.
items.fix: Add the turkey slices to the gravy for the last 2 minutes of cooking so they warm through gently.
